findings.summary: onError returns `maybeError` instead of the resolved `error`, so the single-arg shape loses the error on rethrow.
findings.mechanism: For `onError(err)` (single-arg shape), `maybeError` is `undefined` while `error` (computed above) correctly resolves to `connectionOrError`. The final `return maybeError as Promise<void>` returns `undefined` in this case instead of `error`, so `throw this.onError(e)` in the SDK rethrows `undefined` rather than the real error — exactly the regression the change's comments say it exists to prevent. Only the two-arg shape (`onError(connection, err)`) happens to work correctly since there `maybeError === error`.
